title: Optimizing Logistics Route Selection
business: A regional logistics provider managing last-mile delivery fleets.
problem: The company faces an exponential increase in potential delivery route combinations as the number of stops per vehicle grows, making exhaustive search computationally prohibitive for real-time dispatching.
solution: Branch and Bound prunes optimization search using bounds on the best possible descendant solution, allowing the system to discard entire sub-trees of route combinations that cannot possibly improve upon the current best-known path.
steps: Define the state space as a tree where each node represents a partial delivery route.
Calculate a lower bound cost for each partial route using a heuristic function that estimates the remaining distance.
Explore the tree using a search strategy, maintaining a global variable for the best complete solution found so far.
Prune any branch where the lower bound exceeds the current best complete solution cost.
Terminate when all remaining branches are either pruned or fully explored to guarantee the optimal route.
outcome: The system achieves optimal route selection significantly faster than brute force by ignoring non-viable path segments.
limitation: The efficiency of the algorithm is highly dependent on the quality of the lower bound heuristic; a weak bound results in minimal pruning and performance degradation, which can be checked by monitoring the ratio of explored nodes versus total possible nodes.
